title: Group and cache with computeIfAbsent

blocks.text: `Map.computeIfAbsent(key, function)` is "get or compute" in one call: it runs `function` only when `key` is missing, stores the result and returns the value now in the map. It replaces the get-check-put dance.
Write two methods in `Groups`; `computeIfAbsent` is the page's tool for both:

items: `byFirstLetter(List<String> words)` returns a map from a lower-case first letter to the words starting with it, in their original order.
`lengthOf(Map<String, Integer> cache, String word, Function<String, Integer> measure)` returns the cached value for `word`, measuring and caching it first if needed.

blocks.text: Measuring can be expensive, so it must happen at most once per word. The cache key is the word exactly as given (`"Hello"` and `"hello"` are two keys). Words may start with a capital, and a word may be empty (length 0): an empty word is skipped, and every other word is grouped under its first character lower-cased, whatever that character is, a space included.

cases.says: Words are grouped under their first letter, in the order they came.
The measured value is returned and stored in the cache.
The measuring Function runs only for a word the cache does not hold yet.
Upper- and lower-case first letters share one group, keyed by the lower-case letter.
An empty word has no first letter and is left out.
The cache is looked up by equals, so an equal word built separately is found without measuring again.
A word that starts with a space is not empty: it is grouped under the space character.
The cache is keyed by the word exactly as given, so Hello and hello are measured and stored separately.

concepts: Map.computeIfAbsent runs its Function only for a missing key, stores the result and returns the value.
